text:
Ava (People Ops): Quick Q — booking a biz trip with two overnights in different countries. How do we do per-diem and foreign-card receipts?
Sam (Finance): Short answer: use per-diem rules per overnight location, and submit local receipts plus the card statement for FX.
Diego: So if I fly to Berlin (overnight) then Paris (overnight) in one trip, do I claim two different per-diems?
Sam (Finance): Yes — per-diem is applied by date & overnight location. For each calendar day, use the rate tied to the country where the overnight was spent.
Ava (People Ops): What about partial days? e.g., travel day arrives at 11pm or leaves at 6am.
Priya (Travel Ops): We prorate on travel days: if you were traveling and didn’t have an overnight at a location, follow the travel-day prorate table in the policy (short/long travel day). If you had an overnight, that night’s country rate applies.
Diego: Currency conversions — I paid with my personal EUR card for one hotel and company card for the other. Do I need both receipts?
Sam (Finance): Yes. Required: itemized hotel folio for each stay (showing nights, tax), and the card statement or payment confirmation that shows the charge. For personal card charges in foreign currency, include the card statement or a FX conversion screenshot. Enter both local-amount and USD equivalent on the expense.
Ava (People Ops): Are meal receipts still required if using per-diem?
Sam (Finance): For per-diem claims, you generally do NOT need itemized meal receipts for standard per-diem days. Exceptions: any single meal > company per-meal cap, alcohol, or a non-reimbursable line item — those need receipts and explanation. If you choose to submit actual receipts instead of per-diem, Finance will reimburse actuals but requires full itemized receipts and may take longer to process.
Priya (Travel Ops): Also note: company card meals that are charged as group/team dinners need attendee list and allocation notes if splitting.
Diego: Tip policy for international meals?
Sam (Finance): Tipping is allowed up to 20% unless local custom differs. Add tip as a separate line on the receipt where possible. If tip is embedded, show the full itemized receipt.
Ava (People Ops): Any special file naming or fields for multi-currency?
ExpenseBot: Please include these fields in the expense form: date, local_amount (with currency code), usd_equivalent, exchange_rate_source (card/provider or xe.com screenshot), receipt_upload (one per charge), notes (city/night allocation).
Diego: Example?
Priya (Travel Ops): Example block you can paste into notes:
```
Expense split: 2026-05-12 Berlin (overnight 1) - 75.00 EUR (hotel folio ID 12345)
2026-05-13 Paris (overnight 2) - 92.00 EUR (hotel folio ID 54321)
Conversion: card rate 1 EUR = 1.09 USD on transaction date
Attendees (dinner): Diego, Priya, Alex
```
Sam (Finance): For hotels, taxes and city fees are reimbursable. If you booked a non-refundable personal rate to save money, put that in notes — Finance may reimburse up to the company-standard rate.
Ava (People Ops): How long to file after return?
Sam (Finance): File within 30 days. If you miss 30 days, include a quick note explaining delay; longer delays may require manager approval.
Diego: Anything else for multi-city trips?
Priya (Travel Ops): If you switch time zones and cross-dates, use local dates for each overnight. If in doubt, ping travel-ops with itinerary screenshot.
Ava (People Ops): Awesome — can you link the policy doc?
ExpenseBot: Policy link: https://redwood.company/policies/travel-expense (see sections: per-diem rates, FX, receipts). :thumbsup:
Diego: Thanks all — will submit with both folios and card statements.
Sam (Finance): Thanks — tag me if expense needs manual review. :white_check_mark:
